chunks.arabic_text: غَيْبَةُ النُّعْمَانِيِّ: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ الْحِميريّ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى بْنِ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ يَقْطِينَ، عَنِ النُّضْرِ بْنِ سَوِيدٍ، عَنْ يَحْيَى الْحَلَبِيِّ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ قَالَ

translations.en: Ghayba of al-Nu'mani: Muhammad ibn Abdallah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd ibn Yaqtin, from al-Nadhr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza who said:

chunks.arabic_text: كُنْتُ مَعَ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ، وَمَعَنَا مَوْلًى لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ الْبَاقِرِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ فَقَالَ: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ يَقُولُ: مِنَّا اثْنَا عَشَرَ مُحَدَّثًا، السَّابِعُ مِنْ وَلَدِي الْقَائِمُ، فَقَامَ إِلَيْهِ أَبُو بَصِيرٍ فَقَالَ: أَشْهَدُ أَنِّي سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ يَقُولُهُ مُنْذُ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً

translations.en: I was with Abu Basir, and there was a freed-slave of Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) with us, so he said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: From us are twelve Muhadathun, the seventh of my descendants is the Qaim. So Abu Basir stood up facing him and said: I bear witness that I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying that forty years ago.

en.summary: This narration from Al-Nu'mani's *Ghayba* explicitly identifies the seventh Imam, Muhammad al-Baqir, as the progenitor of the Qaim (Mahdi), anchoring the doctrine of Occultation in the lineage of the Ahl al-Bayt. The term 'Muhadathun' underscores the unique epistemological status of the Imams as recipients of divine inspiration, while Abu Basir’s forty-year testimony provides crucial historical continuity and authenticity to this eschatological claim within Shia scholarship.
en.seo_question: Who is the Qaim among the twelve Muhadathun according to Imam al-Baqir?

key_terms.مُحَدَّثًا: Muhadathun (plural of Muhadath, meaning those who converse with God)
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: Al-Qaim (The Riser, a title for the Mahdi)
